comparison: M_A vs M_B (does L add predictive power?) vs M_C (does L x D add more?), evaluated zero-refit on held-out long-L cells using log-loss/Brier/MAE + Spearman.

stats.meanAtL(D): mean acc over D in {4,8} at length L

decision_rule.threshold_justification: binomial diff-of-means SE ~0.32 at n=5, so 0.15 is a GO/NO-GO on an AGGREGATE (not per-cell); 0.20 sits above noise and is resolvable at n>=10-20 (the 12B confirmation).

honesty: n=5 screening => Stage-A verdicts PRELIMINARY; only 12B confirms.
S=medium only (S robustness deferred to Phase 13).
We do NOT assume longer is worse; A, B and C are all live.
length token-exact => filler/query/evidence/decoys matched; L is the only variable across the L axis.

models.desc: competition only; L ignored (length never harms)
models.name: M_A  F(log(1+D), S)

models.desc: additive length term (length harms regardless of D)
models.name: M_B  F(log(1+D), S, L)

models.desc: competition x length interaction (competition more damaging as L grows)
models.name: M_C  F(log(1+D), S, L, log(1+D) x L)

name: phase12a_longctx_screen_v1

outcomes.A: Long-context penalty exists: L x D term negative and confirmed -> supports 'effective context' thesis (R = F(task, domain, log(1+D), S, L) with a harmful L interaction).
outcomes.B: Length matters ONLY under competition: D=0 stays flat at long L but D>0 degrades -> large context is not inherently unreliable; it becomes unreliable when it contains competing evidence.
outcomes.C: Length barely matters: no L term / interaction survives -> context COMPOSITION, not length, is the dominant reliability variable.

question: Does increasing context length create a reproducible reliability penalty, especially under competition (L x D interaction)?
